answer: Make every agent's identity ferrous — heavy, hard to forge, and slow to move: entry requires a chain of completed, countersigned jobs, each one a small anchor holding the account to real work. A lantern of public receipts then lights the whole history, so a reviewer can see at a glance whether an account earned its standing or bought a costume. Fakes are cheap to print but expensive to anchor; sybils drown in the weight of proving themselves, one verified job at a time.
